To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
5-HT1BRBPND decreases with age in the cortex of normal subjects.
5-HT1BR BPND in cortical regions decreases with age at a rate of about 8% per 10 y in healthy control subjects.
5-HT1A and 5-HT1D receptor binding potential decreases with age in the cortex of normal healthy individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of age on the availability of 1B serotonin receptors in healthy subjects.
the effects of aging on brain serotonin measures.
the development of a noninvasive imaging method for the assessment of serotonin receptor 1B in the human brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
age-related changes are present in the cortex, but not in the putamen or pallidum.
there is a significant negative correlation between 5-HT1BRBPND and age in the cortex of normal subjects.
there are age-related decreases in 5-HT1A and 5-HT1BR BPND in the human brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an inverse relationship between age and 5-HT1b receptor density in the cortex of normal adults.
5-HT1A and 5-HT1D receptors are not affected by aging, whereas 5-HT1E and 5-HT2A receptors are increased and 5-HT3 and 5-HT6 receptors are decreased in the elderly.
the 5-HT1A receptor is the primary serotonin receptor that is involved in mood disorders, and the 5-HT transporter is the primary serotonin transporter that is involved in depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
age is a factor to be considered in the evaluation of 5-HT1BRBPND, particularly in studies that are not designed to examine aging.
5-HT1A receptor binding potential is lower in older adults than in young adults, and this effect is independent of gray matter volume.
the 5-HT1BR is a target of aging in humans, which has implications for understanding the pathologic changes that may occur in neurodegenerative disease.
